analysis:
All four units are documentation only: two CHANGELOG.md head excerpts (lines 874+ and 1266+) and the docs/provider/cli-reference.md patch. The only visible diff is the stamp date bump and a new note at the LaunchAgent environment passthrough section. The note says TMPDIR selects the anonymous runtime metallib snapshot directory for sandboxed foreground/local startup, that it is not forwarded to the background provider, and it links to the configuration.md#runtime-metallib-snapshots anchor. No code changed in the supplied units, so no concrete regression can be shown. The note does describe an environment-influenced path used when loading a runtime metallib. The implementing source and the TB-003 and T-013 binary-integrity and tamper analysis are not supplied. The next pass should check that the TMPDIR path is validated, that snapshots are anonymous and not operator-replaceable, and that runtime-manifest hash checks still apply.

The CHANGELOG excerpts are full head text, not a patch, so the lines this PR changed cannot be identified. Several entries touch the T-041 and TB-007 prefix-cache surface and are not covered by the T-041 text. These are complete Qwen prefix checkpoints on encrypted SSD by default, including recurrent state, MTP history and an MoE codec. They also include network prefix caching with an operator allowlist, content-indexed prefix holders across machine epochs, cache-credit routing, and SSD telemetry in heartbeats. T-041 describes the SSD tier as attention KV blocks only, with HMAC-keyed names, a 30-minute TTL, and a disk budget of available-disk/2 with no fixed ceiling. One changelog entry says the default ceiling is 100 GiB, limited to half of available space. That conflicts with the threat-model statement of no fixed ceiling, but it may be pre-existing text and cannot be attributed to this PR. If the implementing PRs are in this change set, T-041 and TB-007 likely need updating for recurrent-state checkpoints, cross-machine prefix-holder indexing, and cache-based routing credit as a timing and enumeration oracle. This is a coverage limit, not a finding.
